cards.front: A 26-year-old has five or six periods a year and hirsutism; free testosterone is raised. TSH, prolactin and 17-hydroxyprogesterone are normal, and transvaginal ultrasound shows normal ovaries. The diagnosis is [___].
cards.context:
Rotterdam criteria need two of three: ovulatory dysfunction, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovarian morphology, after excluding mimics.

She meets the first two, so normal ovaries on ultrasound do not exclude the diagnosis.

cards.front: A woman with a uterus asks her GP for compounded bioidentical hormones to treat hot flushes. She is advised against them partly because compounded progesterone may not adequately protect her [___].
cards.context:
The Australasian Menopause Society advises against compounded bioidentical hormones: dosing and purity lack regulatory assurance, and evidence of efficacy and safety is lacking.

Unopposed estrogen can cause endometrial hyperplasia and cancer. Compounded progesterone may not provide adequate protection for women with a uterus.

Regulated body-identical MHT is available in Australia, including estradiol and micronised progesterone.

cards.front: Swyer syndrome is complete gonadal dysgenesis in a person with a [___] karyotype.
cards.context:
In 46,XY complete gonadal dysgenesis the gonads never become testes, so they make neither testosterone nor anti-Müllerian hormone.

Without anti-Müllerian hormone the uterus and tubes develop normally, and the external genitalia are female.
